entities.summary:
The Internet Archive, founded in 1996 by Brewster Kahle, stands as a monumental institution in the realm of digital preservation and access to information. Headquartered in San Francisco, California, it has pioneered efforts to archive the vast expanse of the World Wide Web, aiming to provide universal access to all knowledge. This non-profit organization plays a critical role in safeguarding the cultural and historical artifacts of the digital age, ensuring that the fleeting nature of online content does not result in permanent loss. Its mission aligns with the broader trends of democratizing information in an increasingly digital world, making it a significant player in the ongoing narrative of human history.

Through its flagship project, the Wayback Machine, the Internet Archive allows users to view archived versions of web pages dating back to 1996, a feat that has resulted in billions of archived pages. By 2023, the Internet Archive had amassed over 600 billion web pages, acting as a repository for researchers, historians, and the general public to access the past as it existed online. The organization also expands its reach through various initiatives including the Open Library, which offers millions of books for free, and the Archive of Digital Art, showcasing the evolution of digital creativity. These efforts mark significant contributions to the preservation of digital culture and the accessibility of information.
